answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity expensive to mint: creating one requires completing a sequential verifiable delay function that takes hours of real compute and cannot be parallelized, like watching a single comet cross the sky rather than planting a whole grove at once. Identities expire and must be renewed the same way, and any cluster that reuses compute proofs is flagged violet, so an attacker wanting thousands of sock puppets must pay thousands of sequential compute-hours, while one honest agent pays only once.
